To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the adventitious carbon layer on the surface of all samples exposed to air is not a single component, but is a mixture of hydrocarbons and hydrocarbon oxides, and the composition varies from sample to sample; (2) the C 1 s spectra of adventitious carbon are not universal and cannot be used to calibrate BEs of all samples; (3) the C 4f spectra of adventitious hydrocarbon oxides are not universal, and their BEs vary

the adventitious carbon layer on the surface is a complex mixture of hydrocarbons and oxygenates with the C 1 s BE ranging from ∼ 283.0 eV to ∼ 286.0 eV, depending on the sample composition, the sample history, and the experimental conditions; the BE of the C 1S peak of the adventitious layer on the surface of a sample is not constant and is a function of the sample history, sample composition, and experimental conditions;
the adventitious carbon layer is composed of a mixture of hydrocarbons, which can be oxidized in air and, thus, can have different chemical states.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: the origin of the C 1 s BE reference; its stability and reproducibility; and the influence of the sample surface on the C  1s BE.

the following issues: (i) the origin of the adventitious C 1s signal; (ii) the effect of sample charging on the C 3s and C 1s binding energies; (iii) the influence of the C 1 s BE on the interpretation of the XPS spectrum; and (iv) the effect of the C 3 s BE on the C 2 p BE.
the development of a reliable BE referencing method for XPS and related techniques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the adventitious carbon method is the only method available for the calibration of the BE scale in XPS, but its use is highly arbitrary and can lead to significant errors in the interpretation of XPS spectra.
the adventitious carbon method is the most reliable and robust approach to BE referencing in XPS.
C 1s is not a reliable BE reference.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BE referencing procedure is not as simple as it seems.
the C 1 s BE of adventitious carbon should not be used as a reference for BE calibration.
the adventitious carbon method, if used correctly, is a valid and reliable method to calibrate the XPS binding energy scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C 1 s peak of adventitious hydrocarbon should not be used as a reference for BE calibration.
, despite the many problems associated with C  1s referencing, this method remains the most practical approach to BE referencing.
the adventitious carbon layer on a surface should be considered as a contaminant, which is to be minimized and avoided in XPS analysis.
